item.description: By MICHAEL R. SISAK, DAVID B. CARUSO and LARRY NEUMEISTER Associated Press NEW YORK (AP) — The FBI pored over Jeffrey Epstein’s bank records and emails. It searched his homes. item.title: Washington Post Publisher Will Lewis Says He’s Stepping Down, Days After Big Layoffs At The Paper
item.description: By DAVID BAUDER AP Media Writer Washington Post publisher Will Lewis said Saturday that he’s stepping down, ending a troubled tenure three days after the newspaper said that it was laying off one-third of its staff. Lewis announced his departure in a two-paragraph email to the newspaper’s staff, saying that after two years of transformation, “now is the right time for me to step aside.” The Post’s chief financial officer, Jeff D’Onofrio, was appointed temporary publisher. item.title: Police Arrest Protesters At Minneapolis Federal Building On 1-Month Anniversary Of Woman’s Death
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Several dozen protesters were arrested Saturday outside a federal building in Minneapolis, breaking up a protest marking the one-month anniversary of a Minnesota woman’s death at the hands of an immigration officer. Renee Good was killed on Jan. 7 as she was driving away from immigration officers in a Minneapolis neighborhood. item.description: By SAFIYAH RIDDLE Associated Press President Donald Trump’s administration can continue to detain immigrants without bond, marking a major legal victory for the federal immigration agenda and countering a slew of recent lower court decisions across the country that argued the practice is illegal. item.title: Ohio Man Charged With Threatening To Kill Vice President JD Vance And Possessing Child Abuse Files
item.description: By JOSH FUNK Associated Press An Ohio man has been charged with threatening to kill Vice President JD Vance while he was visiting his home state last month. But the man’s lawyer said his health makes it unlikely he would have been able to carry out the threat. item.title: Russian Airstrike On Ukrainian City Kills 1 As US Pushes June Deadline For Peace Deal
item.description: (AP) — A Russian airstrike on a residential area in eastern Ukraine killed one person and wounded two, officials said Sunday, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the U.S. has given Ukraine and Russia a June deadline to reach a peace deal.
